newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sees little impact from Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Australia sees little impact from Deng's death.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Thursday said Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping's death would have little impact on Beijing's international relations.
"I don't expect it will make a fundamental change to either relations between Australia and China or relations between China and the rest of the world," Howard said in a radio interview.

"China wants to have good relations despite the vast differences between her political system and that of the rest of the Western world -- that will go on," said Howard, who is due to visit Beijing next month.
"The most interesting thing will be to watch any realignment of power influences by the people who are now completely in charge," he said.
Howard and other government leaders hailed Deng's economic reforms, which they said helped transform China and had fuelled economic growth in the Asia-Pacific region.
"He is the person who more than anybody else modernised China's economy, so his economic legacy is a very powerful one," Howard said.
Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer said Deng's economic reforms had benefited the region and China had lost a historic figure.

"We owe a great deal to Deng Xiaoping because of course the knock-on of that (economic reform) has reached far beyond China and contributed to economic growth right across this part of the world," Fischer said.
Sino-Australian relations had chilled under Australia's year-old conservative government, but Howard and Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said ties were improving and would continue to strengthen.
Downer said Canberra was not concerned about a possible power struggle in the wake of Deng's death.
"We don't see any immediate changes in China," Downer said in a radio interview from the Papua New Guinea capital, Port Moresby, where he is on an official visit.

"The Chinese leadership have been making preparations for his death for a long time and in recent times the Chinese leaders have really reaffirmed the economic path that Deng had laid out, so we wouldn't expect any immediate changes," he said.
